html:
Mandatory Palestine was the territory between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean that Britain ruled from 1920 to 1948, under a mandate of the League of Nations. The map shows it from 1920 to 1938.

Britain took the land from the Ottomans in 1917. That year the Balfour Declaration promised support for a "national home for the Jewish people" in Palestine, while also promising to protect the rights of the Arab majority. The mandate wrote this promise in. Land east of the Jordan was split off as the Emirate of Transjordan.

Jewish immigration, driven by Zionism and then by persecution in Europe, raised the Jewish share of the population from about a tenth to about a third. Arab fears of losing their land led to riots in 1929 and the Arab revolt of 1936 to 1939.

After 1945 Britain handed the problem to the United Nations, which voted for partition in November 1947. Civil war followed. The mandate ended on 14 May 1948, when Israel declared independence and hundreds of thousands of Palestinians fled or were driven out in the Nakba.
sum: Mandatory Palestine was the territory between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean that Britain ruled from 1920 to 1948, under a mandate of the League of Nations. The map shows it from 1920 to 1938.
